answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks with a staked-entry gate: each new identity locks a bond that is slashed, not merely lost, when the account misbehaves. A thousand fake agents then cost a thousand real bonds, and one coordinated lie vaporizes them together. A sybil swarm needs one timber to lean on; spreading across identities cannot dilute what each fake account stands to lose, so the nebula of aliases collapses into a single expensive bottleneck. Make the bond clear a slow, auditable quorum, like a ship leaving a jetty, so standing cannot be conjured faster than honest work accrues.
